statement.text:
Let G be a group, and φ an automorphism of G. Elements x, y ∈ G are said
to be φ-conjugate if x = z −1 yφ(z) for some z ∈ G. The φ-conjugacy is an equivalence
relation; the number of φ-conjugacy classes is denoted by R(φ).
    Conjecture: If a finitely generated residually finite group G has an automorphism
φ such that R(φ) is finite, then G has a soluble subgroup of finite index.
    The conjecture is proved if φ has prime order (E. Jabara, J. Algebra, 320, no. 10
(2008), 3671–3679). If G is infinitely generated, then G does not have to be almost
solvable (K. Dekimpe, D. Gonçalves, Bull. London Math. Soc., 46, no. 4 (2014), 737–
746), but if it is of finite upper rank, then it has to be almost solvable (E. Troitsky,
J. Group Theory, 28, no. 1 (2025), 151–164).               A. L. Fel’shtyn, E. V. Troitsky
